english.title: Use title without entry in the register
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), used at a pharmacy, namely **(..SPECIFY PHARMACY..)

(A)_[the title 'pharmacist' without being entered as a pharmacist in part 1 or 4 of the register]_
(B)_[the title 'pharmacy technician' without being entered as a pharmacy technician in part 2 or 5 of the register]_
(C)_[a prescribed specialist title in respect of a particular annotation namely **(..SPECIFY TITLE..) in that you did not have an entry in any part of the register with that particular annotation]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 38(2) and (8) of the Pharmacy Order 2010.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see Article 38(10)Note
(i) Article 38(10) states: Proceedings for an offence under this article may be begun at any time within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Council to justify a prosecution came to the Council's knowledge; but no proceedings may be begun after the expiry of the period of two years beginning with the date of the commission of the offence.
(ii) Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
